title: Night Sky Walk — Coastal Dark Site
summary: Guided naked-eye tour of seasonal constellations, planets, and the Milky Way under darker suburban skies.
description: Meet at the coastal viewpoint for a two-hour walk. Bring warm layers and a red torch. Telescopes are optional; binoculars welcome. We cover constellation mythology, how to find planets, and how to use Astro Walk on your phone for live orientation.
skyHint: Look south after twilight for Jupiter and the brighter winter stars.

title: Solar Filter Workshop
summary: Learn safe solar observing, filter fitting, and how to book kit for the next transit.
description: Hands-on session covering white-light filters, alignment, and common mistakes. Includes a short imaging stack demo. Suitable for beginners who already own a small refractor or want to try club gear.
skyHint: Daytime event — open Astro Walk later that night for planets.

title: Meteor Watch Campout
summary: Overnight meteor watch with counting sheets, hot drinks, and a dawn planet check.
description: Arrive before midnight, claim a spot on the field, and log meteors with our coordinators. Breakfast after dawn. Tents optional; cars allowed in the outer lot. Children welcome with a guardian.
skyHint: Use Astro Walk to face the radiant and keep dark-adapted eyes.

title: Saturn Night — Public Telescope
summary: Ringed planet at the eyepiece plus a short talk on moons and the Cassini Division.
description: Club scopes will be collimated on Saturn. Queue is time-boxed so everyone gets a view. Astro Walk can help you find Saturn before you reach the queue.
skyHint: Search Saturn in Astro Walk, then follow the guide arrows.
